q: Per RA 9266 Sec. 31, how does the law characterize an unregistered person soliciting architectural work?
o: As lawful so long as no contract is actually signed
Study first pa muna po
As permissible marketing activity distinct from practice
As offering to practice architecture, which is unlawful for non-registered and unlicensed persons to do
As a purely civil matter with no penal consequence
n: Section 31 states "solicitation of architectural work shall be construed as offering to practice architecture and shall be unlawful for any non-registered and unlicensed persons to do so." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 31)

q: Under Sec. 26 (Vested Rights) of RA 9266, what happens to architects already registered before the law took effect?
o: They must retake the licensure exam under the new subjects
Their prior registrations are voided, requiring a fresh application

They are automatically registered under the new Act, subject to future requirements, with existing Certificates of Registration in good standing carrying the same force as if issued after the Act's passage
They must pay a one-time fee equal to double the usual registration fee
n: Section 26 provides all previously registered architects "shall automatically be registered under the provisions hereof, subject...to the provisions herein set forth as to future requirements," and their certificates "shall have the same force and effect as though issued after the passage of this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 26)

q: Sec. 12 of RA 9266 requires the licensure examination be given at places/dates the Commission designates, in accordance with which other law?
o: Republic Act No. 1581
Republic Act No. 8981
Republic Act No. 7160
Republic Act No. 545
n: Section 12 requires the examination to be given "in such places and dates as the Commission may designate in accordance with the provisions of Republic Act No. 8981." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 12)

q: Which act, under Sec. 23(b) of RA 9266, is grounds for suspending or revoking a Certificate of Registration?
o: Hiring more than five employees in one's firm
Practicing architecture for more than 20 years
Paying money, apart from the regular fees, to secure a Certificate of Registration
Attending more CPD seminars than required
n: Section 23(b) names as a ground "has paid money except the regular fees provided for to secure a Certificate of Registration." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23(b))

q: Per Sec. 8 of RA 9266, which body has custody of all Board records — including exam applications and administrative/investigative case files — and designates the Board Secretary?
o: The local government unit where the Board sits
The Department of Trade and Industry
The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization
The Professional Regulation Commission
n: Section 8 provides that "all records of the Board...shall be under the custody of the Commission," and "the Commission shall designate the Secretary of the Board." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 8)

q: Which RA 9266 term names the architect who is directly and professionally responsible and liable specifically for a project's construction supervision?
o: Consulting Architect
Architecture-in-charge of construction
Architect-of-record
General Practice architect
n: Section 3(2)(b) defines "Architecture-in-charge of construction" as an architect "directly and professionally responsible and liable for the construction supervision of the project." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(2)(b))

q: Sec. 7(l) requires the Board to coordinate with which agency to ensure architecture education meets prescribed curriculum, faculty, library, and facility standards?
o: The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)
The Commission on Higher Education (CHED)
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
n: Section 7(l) empowers the Board, "in coordination with the CHED," to ensure architecture education complies with CHED's policies, standards and requirements on curriculum, faculty, library and facilities. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(l))

q: Under Sec. 18, whose signatures must the Certificate of Registration issued to a passing examinee bear?
o: Only the examinee's college dean
Only the Secretary of Justice
The chairperson of the Commission and the chairman and members of the Board, stamped with the official seal
Only the president of the integrated and accredited professional organization
n: Section 18 states the Certificate of Registration "shall bear the signature of the chairperson of the Commission and the chairman and members of the Board, stamped with the official seal." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 18)

q: How is RA 9266 structurally organized, and which Article addresses examination, registration, and licensure?
o: It has seven Articles; Article V covers examination matters
It has five Articles; Article III covers Examination, Registration and Licensure (Sections 12-28)
It has three Articles; Article II covers examination matters
It has a single, undivided Article covering everything
n: RA 9266 is organized into five Articles: Article I (General Provision), Article II (Professional Regulatory Board), Article III (Examination, Registration and Licensure, Sections 12-28), Article IV (Practice of Architecture, Sections 29-39), and Article V (Final Provisions, Sections 40-47). (Source: RA 9266, Table of Articles)

q: Under Sec. 39, within how many months of the Act's effectivity must the Board, in consultation with the integrated professional organization, implement rules for the professional liability insurance requirement covering foreign nationals under temporary/special permits?
o: Three (3) months
One (1) year
Two (2) years
Six (6) months
n: Section 39 provides these rules "shall be implemented by the Board in consultation with the integrated and accredited professional organization of architects within six (6) months from the effectivity of this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 39)

q: Sec. 5(e) requires a prospective Board member to satisfy which qualification?
o: Must be under 40 years of age
Must hold a foreign architecture license
Must have served as Board Secretary for at least two years
Must never have been convicted of any crime involving moral turpitude
n: Section 5(e) requires that the prospective Board member "has never been convicted of any crime involving moral turpitude." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 5(e))

q: Per Sec. 20(5), all architectural plans, designs, specifications, drawings, and documents relating to a building's construction must bear the seal and signature of whom, plus what identifying details?
o: Any licensed engineer, plus the project's tax declaration number
The building owner, plus the owner's taxpayer identification number
The local government building official, plus the permit control number
Only an architect registered and licensed under the Act, plus his/her professional identification card number and its expiration date
n: Section 20(5) requires that such documents "bear the seal and signature only of an architect registered and licensed under this Act together with his/her professional identification card number and the date of its expiration." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20(5))

q: Which act is a ground for suspension or revocation of a Certificate of Registration under Sec. 23(d)?
o: Taking a one-year leave from active practice
Relocating one's practice to another region
Declining to join the integrated organization's optional committees
Aiding or abetting the practice of architecture by someone not duly authorized to practice in the Philippines
n: Section 23(d) lists as a ground for suspension or revocation that the registrant "has aided or abetted in the practice of architecture any person not duly authorized to practice architecture in the Philippines." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23(d))

q: Under Sec. 33, how are signed, stamped, or sealed drawings, specifications, and other contract documents treated as instruments of service?
o: Property of the government once a building permit issues
Public records open to unrestricted copying
Property of the client immediately upon the down payment
The intellectual property and documents of the architect, whether or not the object they depict is ever built
n: Section 33 provides such documents "are the intellectual property and documents of the architect, whether the object for which they are made is executed or not," and prohibits unauthorized duplication without the architect's written consent. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 33)

q: Which subject does Sec. 14(1) expressly list as covered by the architecture licensure examination?
o: Business Law and Taxation
Comparative Religion and World History
History and Theory of Architecture; Principles of Planning and Architectural Practice
Environmental Science and Chemistry
n: Section 14(1) lists "History and Theory of Architecture; Principles of Planning and Architectural Practice" as one of the subjects covered by the licensure examination. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 14(1))

q: Under Sec. 39, what must foreign nationals (including former Filipinos) wishing to engage in the general practice of architecture locally secure, sized to their project involvement and compensation?
o: A cash deposit with the Bureau of Internal Revenue
A performance bond issued solely by the local government unit
A life insurance policy payable to the Commission
Professional liability insurance or malpractice insurance, or an acceptable equivalent in bond form
n: Section 39 requires such foreign nationals to "secure locally their professional liability insurance or malpractice insurance or their acceptable equivalent in bond form commensurate with the nature and magnitude of their project involvement and their compensation." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 39)

q: A foreign architect entering the country to work on a foreign-funded government project must, under Sec. 38, first secure what before assuming duties?
o: Only a certificate from his home country's embassy
Nothing, since foreign-funded projects are exempt from RA 9266
Only a Bureau of Immigration work visa, without PRC involvement
A special/temporary permit from the Board, subject to Commission approval
n: Section 38 requires foreign nationals performing such services to, "before assuming the duties, functions and responsibilities as architects or consultants, secure a special/temporary permit from the Board subject to approval of the Commission." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38)

q: Under Sec. 31, if a firm tries to dodge the Act by having an unregistered representative or employee solicit architectural work on its behalf, what is the legal effect?
o: No liability attaches unless construction is actually completed
Both the represented party and the representative — employer and employee alike — are deemed guilty of violating the Act
The firm faces only an administrative fine, no criminal liability
Only the unregistered representative, not the firm, is held liable
n: Section 31 provides that in such a scheme, "both those represented and representative, the employer and the employee shall be deemed guilty of violation of this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 31)

q: Before a former teaching faculty member of an architecture school, institute, university, or review center can qualify for Board membership, Sec. 5(d) requires what?
o: Nothing — faculty members automatically qualify
Merely halving the teaching load for one year
A signed waiver from the school president
Officially resigning and completely stopping teaching, advising, or reviewing activities for at least five (5) years before the nomination
n: Section 5(d) disqualifies faculty members from Board membership "unless he/she had officially resigned from such an institution and has completely stopped teaching, advising or reviewing activities for at least five (5) years prior to the nomination." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 5(d))

q: Per Sec. 20(1), for how long may plans prepared by, or under the direct supervision of, a registered architect be stamped with that architect's seal?
o: Only until the building permit is approved
Only for one (1) year after the seal was issued
Indefinitely, even after the certificate is revoked
For the life of the registrant's certificate
n: Section 20(1) provides plans "shall be stampede [stamped] with said seal during the life of the registrant's certificate," and makes it unlawful to use the seal after the certificate has expired or been revoked unless renewed or reissued. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20(1))

q: Under Sec. 38(c), foreign nationals holding a temporary/special permit must work with what, and remain responsible for what?
o: No local counterpart at all
Only members of their own foreign firm
A Filipino counterpart, remaining responsible for public utilities and taxes owed to the Philippine government related to their project participation
Only representatives of the foreign embassy
n: Section 38(c) requires "that foreign nationals shall be required to work with a Filipino counterpart and shall also be responsible for public utilities and taxes due to the Philippine government, relative to their participation in, or professional services rendered to the project." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38(c))

q: Which event, under Sec. 9(c), gives the President grounds to suspend or remove a Board member?
o: Publishing a scholarly article critical of the Board
Voluntary resignation from the integrated organization
Final judgment for crimes involving moral turpitude
Attending an international architecture conference
n: Section 9(c) lists "final judgment of crimes involving moral turpitude" as a ground for suspension or removal of a Board member. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 9(c))

q: Which examination subject, per Sec. 14(2), covers structural design and building materials?
o: Architectural Design and Site Planning
Urban Design and Architectural Interiors
History and Theory of Architecture
Structural Design, Building Materials, and Architectural Specifications, and Methods of Construction and Utilities
n: Section 14(2) lists "Structural Design, Building Materials, and Architectural Specifications, and Methods of Construction and Utilities" as one of the examination subjects. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 14(2))

q: Under Sec. 16, within how many calendar days after the licensure exam must the Board report candidates' ratings to the Commission, absent an extension for just cause?
o: Sixty (60) calendar days
Twenty (20) calendar days
Fifteen (15) calendar days
Thirty (30) calendar days
n: Section 16 requires the Board to submit ratings "within thirty (30) calendar days after the examination, unless extended for just cause." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 16)

q: Per Sec. 22, can registration be refused, or a name struck from the roster, solely due to a conviction for a purely political offense?
o: Yes, but only if the conviction post-dates registration
No, since Sec. 22 applies only to foreign nationals
No — Sec. 22's proviso bars refusing registration or removing a name from the roster over a political-offense conviction, or one that shouldn't disqualify the person in the Board's judgment
Yes, any criminal conviction whatsoever bars registration automatically
n: Section 22 provides "that registration shall not be refused and a name shall not be removed from the roster of architects on conviction for a political offense or for an offense which should not, in the opinion of the Board...disqualify a person from practicing under this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 22)

q: Sec. 32 makes it unlawful for an architect to sign or seal plans made under another architect's supervision unless the signature clearly shows what?
o: The name of the client only
The signing architect's home address
The signing architect's Board exam score
The part or parts of the work actually performed by the signing architect
n: Section 32 requires that any such signature be made "in such manner as to clearly indicate the part or parts of such work actually performed by the former." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 32)

q: What educational credential does Sec. 5(b) require of a Board member?
o: A vocational certificate in drafting
A doctorate in civil engineering
A master's degree in business administration
A Bachelor of Science in Architecture degree from a school, college, or university recognized/accredited by CHED
n: Section 5(b) requires a Board member to "be a holder of a degree in Bachelor of Science in Architecture conferred by a school, college or university in the Philippines or abroad that is recognized and/or accredited by the Commission on Higher Education (CHED)." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 5(b))

q: Sec. 3(4)(i) describes the practice of architecture's scope as covering works serving what overall purpose?
o: The licensing of civil engineers and allied professionals
The financial auditing of construction companies
The exclusive marketing of construction materials
The scientific, aesthetic, and orderly coordination of all works needed to produce a complete building or structure, safeguarding life, health, and property and promoting quality of life
n: Section 3(4)(i) covers "all works which relate to the scientific, aesthetic and orderly coordination of all works and branches of the work, systems and process necessary for the production of a complete building or structure...in order to enhance and safeguard life, health and property and the promotion and enrichment of the quality of life." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(i))

q: Sec. 41 states the implementing rules and regulations themselves take effect how many days after publication in the Official Gazette or two major newspapers?
o: Thirty (30) days
Sixty (60) days
Ten (10) days
Fifteen (15) days
n: Section 41 states the IRR "shall be effective fifteen (15) days following their publication in the Official Gazette or in two (2) major daily newspapers of general circulation." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 41)

q: An examinee holds a Bachelor of Science in Architecture and a Master's Degree in Architecture from a government-recognized school, but only one actual year of diversified experience. Does Sec. 13(c) qualify this person for the exam?
o: No, holding a Master's Degree disqualifies an applicant outright
No, two full years of actual experience are required with no possible credit
Yes, but only if the applicant is over 30
Yes — Sec. 13(c) credits one year of experience for a recognized Master's Degree in Architecture, which combined with the one actual year satisfies the two-year requirement
n: Section 13(c) requires two (2) years of diversified experience but provides "an applicant holding a Master's Degree in Architecture from a school, college, university or institute recognized by the government shall be credited one (1) year in his/her practical experience," so one actual year plus the one-year credit satisfies the requirement. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 13(c))

q: Per Sec. 35, within how many years of the Act's effectivity must government positions primarily requiring an architect's services be filled only by registered and licensed architects?
o: Ten (10) years
Five (5) years
One (1) year
Three (3) years
n: Section 35 provides that "within (3) years from the effectivity of this Act, all existing and proposed positions in the local and national government...primarily requiring the services of an architect shall be filled only by registered and licensed architects." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 35)

q: A private developer forces a registered architect to render general-practice services without first executing a written contract or service agreement. Per Sec. 30, what fine and imprisonment range applies upon conviction?
o: Not less than P50,000.00, imprisonment up to three (3) years
No fine, only imprisonment up to one (1) year
Not less than P1,000,000.00, imprisonment up to ten (10) years
Not less than P200,000.00, imprisonment up to six (6) years
n: Section 30 penalizes any person or entity that forces an architect to perform services "without first executing a written contract/service agreement" with "a fine of not less than Two hundred thousand pesos (P200,000.00) or...imprisonment for a period not exceeding six (6) years, or both." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 30)

q: Aside from being signed by the Commission's chairperson, what does the Professional Identification Card show under Sec. 18?
o: The examinee's college GPA
The names of all Board members at the time of exam
The examinee's home address only
The registration number, date of issuance, and expiry date
n: Section 18 provides that the Professional Identification Card bears "the registration number, date of issuance, expiry date, duly signed by the chairperson of the Commission." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 18)

q: Which prior law does Sec. 46 (Repealing Clause) expressly repeal?
o: Republic Act No. 8981, the PRC Modernization Act
Republic Act No. 545, as amended by Republic Act No. 1581, otherwise known as 'An Act to Regulate the Practice of Architecture in the Philippines'
Presidential Decree No. 1096, the National Building Code
Republic Act No. 1581, standing alone
n: Section 46 provides "Republic Act No. 545, as amended by Republic Act No. 1581 is hereby repealed," and the Act's title also identifies RA 545 as "An Act to Regulate the Practice of Architecture in the Philippines." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 46 (see also the Act's title))

q: Which of these is NOT actually listed among Sec. 13's stated qualifications for an examination applicant?
o: Not having been convicted of a crime involving moral turpitude
Being a Filipino citizen or qualified foreign citizen per the Act
Being of good moral character
Holding a Master's Degree in Architecture as a mandatory minimum
n: Section 13 requires a Bachelor of Science in Architecture degree plus diversified experience (with a Master's Degree merely crediting one year of experience) — a Master's Degree is not itself a mandatory qualification. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 13)

q: Under Sec. 4, the President appoints Board members from how many recommendees, themselves drawn from how many nominees per position submitted by the integrated professional organization?
o: 1 recommendee from 3 nominees
3 recommendees from 5 nominees
2 recommendees from 4 nominees
5 recommendees from 10 nominees
n: Section 4 provides for appointment "from a lists of three (3) recommendees chosen from a list of five (5) nominees for each position submitted to the Commission by the integrated and the accredited professional organization of architects." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 4)

q: Once an architect registers with the Board, what happens to his/her membership in the integrated professional organization, per Sec. 40?
o: Membership requires passing a separate exam
Membership stays entirely voluntary and separate from registration
The architect automatically becomes a member upon paying required fees/dues, without barring membership in other associations
Membership is reserved only for honors graduates
n: Section 40 provides a registered architect "shall automatically become member of the integrated and accredited professional organization of architects...upon payment of the required fees and dues," and that such membership "shall not be a bar to membership in other associations of architects." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 40)

q: Which of these is explicitly listed under Sec. 3(4) as part of the Scope of the Practice of Architecture?
o: Certification of land titles
Preparation of preliminary, technical, economic, and financial feasibility studies of plans, models, and project promotional services
Adjudication of labor disputes on construction sites
Issuance of building-occupancy tax assessments
n: Section 3(4)(d) includes "preparation of preliminary, technical, economic and financial feasibility studies of plans, models and project promotional services" within the scope of the practice of architecture. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(d))

q: A foreign national with no authority to practice architecture in the Philippines stays in-country and performs the activities described in Sections 3 and 4 in connection with a building's construction. How does Sec. 25 characterize this?
o: As acceptable so long as he/she is merely observing construction
As a lawful courtesy extended to foreign professionals
As a form of consulting exempt from registration
As engaging in the unauthorized practice of architecture
n: Section 25 provides that a foreign architect or unauthorized person performing such activities "shall be deemed engaged in the unauthorized practice of architecture." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 25)

q: Sec. 7(k) gives the Board what power over temporary or special permits?
o: Import permits for construction equipment
Approving, issuing, limiting, or canceling them
Passports for architects traveling abroad
Business licenses for hardware stores
n: Section 7(k) empowers the Board to "approve, issue, limit or cancel temporary or special permit to practice architecture." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(k))

q: Within how many days of the Act's effectivity must the Board, subject to Commission approval and coordinating with the integrated professional organization, adopt and promulgate the IRR and the Code of Ethical Conduct/Standards of Professional Practice, per Sec. 41?
o: Ninety (90) days
Sixty (60) days
Thirty (30) days
Fifteen (15) days
n: Section 41 requires the Board, "within sixty (60) days after the effectivity of this Act," to adopt and promulgate the implementing rules and regulations and the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 41)

q: Sec. 38(b) requires a foreign national seeking a temporary/special permit to satisfy which condition?
o: Sponsorship by at least three Filipino architects
Being legally qualified to practice architecture in his/her own country, with expertise necessary and advantageous to the Philippines particularly for technology transfer and specialization
Exemption from all Philippine taxes during the permit period
Five years of permanent Philippine residency
n: Section 38(b) requires "that he/she is legally qualified to practice architecture in his/her own country, and that his/her expertise is necessary and advantageous to our country particularly in the aspects of technology transfer and specialization." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38(b))

q: Which of these, under Sec. 9(a), grounds the President's power to suspend or remove a Board member?
o: Membership in a review center's faculty
Filing an annual report with the Commission
Being reappointed for a second term
Neglect of duty or incompetence
n: Section 9(a) lists "neglect of duty or incompetence" as a ground for the President, on the Commission's recommendation, to suspend or remove a Board member. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 9(a))

q: Which of these does Sec. 3(4)(h) expressly list as part of the scope of the practice of architecture?
o: Sanitary and mechanical engineering design exclusively
Land surveying and geodetic engineering
Issuance of local-government occupancy permits
Building programming, building administration, construction arbitration, and architectural conservation and restoration
n: Section 3(4)(h) lists "building programming, building administration, construction arbitration and architectural conservation and restoration" as part of the scope of the practice of architecture. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(h))

q: Aside from a fine, Sec. 29 allows a court, in its discretion, to impose imprisonment within what range on a person convicted of unauthorized architectural practice?
o: Life imprisonment
Not less than one (1) year or not exceeding two (2) years
A mandatory flat term of exactly one (1) year
Not less than six (6) months or not exceeding six (6) years
n: Section 29 provides for "imprisonment for a period not less than six (6) months or not exceeding six (6) years, or both, at the discretion of the Court." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29)

q: Under Sec. 40, the profession's national organization must be accredited by the Board and Commission-approved, and registered with the SEC as what kind of entity?
o: A for-profit stock corporation owned by the Board
A government-owned and controlled corporation
A non-profit, non-stock corporation governed by by-laws providing democratic election of officials
A sole proprietorship owned by the Commission chairperson
n: Section 40 requires the integrated organization to be "registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission, as a non-profit, non-stock corporation to [be] governed by by-laws providing for a democratic election of its officials." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 40)

q: If part of the Act is declared unconstitutional, what happens to the rest of it under Sec. 45 (Separability Clause)?
o: The entire Act is voided automatically
Only the remaining provisions of that same Article are voided
The judgment does not affect, invalidate, or impair other parts — it is confined to the clause, provision, paragraph, or part directly at issue
Congress must re-enact the whole Act
n: Section 45 provides such a judgment "shall not affect, invalidate or impair any other part hereof, but such judgment shall be merely confined to the clause, provision, paragraph or part directly involved in the controversy." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 45)

q: RA 9266 is described as a consolidation of which two bills, passed by the House and Senate on January 28 and 29, 2004, respectively?
o: House Bill No. 9266 and Senate Bill No. 545
House Bill No. 1096 and Senate Bill No. 8981
House Bill No. 2710 and Senate Bill No. 5389
House Bill No. 5389 and Senate Bill No. 2710
n: The Act states: "This Act which is a consolidation of House Bill No. 5389 and Senate Bill No. 2710 was finally passed by the House of Representatives and the Senate on January 28 2004 and January 29, 2004, respectively." (Source: RA 9266, Enrolled Bill Notation)

q: Sec. 22 requires the Board to refuse registration to a person who, among other grounds, is what?
o: Someone who studied architecture abroad
Simply younger than 25 years old
A person who scored exactly 70% on the licensure exam
Of unsound mind, or convicted of a crime involving moral turpitude, or guilty of immoral/dishonorable conduct
n: Section 22 bars issuance of the certificate to persons who "falsely sworn or misrepresented" themselves, those "convicted by a court of competent jurisdiction of a criminal offense involving moral turpitude or guilty of immoral and dishonorable conduct," or "any person of unsound mind." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 22)

q: Per Sec. 3(11), all registered Filipino architects are, without barring membership elsewhere, members of what body?
o: The Securities and Exchange Commission
The Professional Regulation Commission's board of directors
The Department of Trade and Industry
The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of architects
n: Section 3(11) defines the "Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization" as "the existing official national organization of all architects of the Philippines in which all registered Filipino architects shall be members without prejudice to membership in other voluntary professional associations." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(11))

q: Who acts as legal adviser to the Commission and Board and renders legal assistance under Sec. 44?
o: Any private law firm the Board hires
The president of the integrated professional organization
The Secretary of Justice or his duly designated representative
The Secretary of Trade and Industry
n: Section 44 provides that "the Secretary of Justice or his duly designated representative shall act as legal adviser to the Commission and the Board and shall render legal assistance as may be necessary." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 44)

q: An architect who signs and seals the plans, specifications, and contract documents and assumes civil liability for a project's total design is called, under RA 9266, what?
o: Consulting Architect
Architecture-in-charge of construction
Authorship architect
Architect-of-record
n: Section 3(2)(a) defines the "Architect-of-record" as the architect "directly and professionally responsible for the total design of the project for the client and who shall assume the civil liability for the plans, specifications and contract documents he/she has signed and sealed." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(2)(a))

q: When a firm, partnership, association, or corporation registers to practice architecture, Sec. 37(c) makes its individual members responsible for what?
o: Only acts committed within the National Capital Region
Only the acts they personally sign, with no collective liability
Nothing, since the firm alone bears all liability
Their individual and collective acts as an entity, as provided by law
n: Section 37(c) provides that "individual members of such firm, partnership association or corporation shall be responsible for their individual and collective acts as an entity and as provided by law." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 37(c))

q: Which forms may an 'Architectural Firm' take under Sec. 3(6), provided it is registered with the proper government agencies?
o: Only a corporation
A sole proprietorship, a partnership, or a corporation
Only a sole proprietorship
Only a cooperative
n: Section 3(6) defines "Architectural Firm" as "a sole proprietorship, a partnership or a corporation registered with the proper government agencies." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(6))

q: Sec. 13(a) requires an examination applicant to establish that he/she is what?
o: A resident of the province where the exam is administered
Employed full-time by a licensed architectural firm
A member of the integrated organization for at least a year
A Filipino citizen or a citizen of a foreign country qualified to sit for the exam as the Act provides
n: Section 13(a) requires the applicant to establish that "he/she is a Filipino citizen or a citizen of a foreign country qualified to take the examination as provided for in this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 13(a))

q: Sec. 6 staggers the first Board's initial terms: chairman for three years, one member for two years, and the remaining member for how long?
o: Four (4) years
One (1) year
Two (2) years, matching the second member
Six (6) months
n: Section 6 states that of the first Board appointed, "one (1) member shall be appointed and hold office as chairman for three (3) years, one (1) member for two (2) years, and one (1) member for one (1) year." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 6)

q: During which Congressional session was RA 9266 enacted, and when was it approved?
o: The Eleventh Congress, First Regular Session; approved January 1, 2003
The Twelfth Congress, First Regular Session; approved March 17, 2005
The Thirteenth Congress, Second Regular Session; approved July 28, 2003
The Twelfth Congress, Third Regular Session; approved March 17, 2004
n: The Act was begun and held by the Twelfth Congress, Third Regular Session, in Metro Manila, and RA 9266 bears the date March 17, 2004 as its approval date, signed by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo. (Source: RA 9266, Preamble/Approval)

q: What power does Sec. 7(d) give the Board over a Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card?
o: Selling it to qualified bidders at auction
Issuing, suspending, revoking, or reinstating it
Only issuing it, with no power over suspension/revocation/reinstatement
Delegating all such actions exclusively to the Commission
n: Section 7(d) empowers the Board to "issue, suspend, revoke, or reinstate the Certificate of Registration and the professional Identification Card for the practice of the architecture profession." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(d))

q: May an unregistered person lawfully collect a fee for architectural services, per Sec. 36?
o: Yes, without restriction
It is unlawful for any unregistered person to do so, except an employee collecting on behalf of a Registered Architect
No, not even a registered architect's employee may collect on his behalf
Yes, provided the fee stays below a set amount
n: Section 36 states "it shall be unlawful for any unregistered person to collect a fee for architectural services except as an employee collecting a fee as representative of a Registered Architect." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 36)

q: Which act, per Sec. 23(c), grounds suspension or revocation of a registrant's certificate?
o: Falsely impersonating a practitioner of like or different name, or practicing under an assumed, fictitious, or corporate name other than one's own
Attending CPD seminars
Charging lower fees than peers in the same city
Declining new clients during a given year
n: Section 23(c) lists as a ground for suspension or revocation that the registrant "has falsely impersonated a practitioner, or former practitioner of alike or different name or has practiced under an assumed, fictitious or corporate name other than that of the registered." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23(c))

q: Under Sec. 6, how long is a Board member's term, and how much further service may follow reappointment?
o: Four years, reappointable indefinitely
Two years, reappointable for one more year
Five years, with no reappointment allowed
Three years, reappointable for one further full three-year term
n: Section 6 provides members "shall hold office for a term of three (3) years ... Each member of the Board may be reappointed for one full term of three (3) years." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 6)

q: Per RA 9266's Statement of Policy, by what means does the State aim to develop competent, virtuous, productive, and well-rounded professional architects?
o: By abolishing the licensure exam in favor of on-the-job assessment
Through inviolable, honest, effective, and credible licensure examinations plus regulatory measures, programs, and activities
Through mandatory foreign training programs only
Through unlimited automatic reciprocity with all foreign architects
n: Section 2 declares that the State shall nurture competent architects "through inviolable, honest, effective and credible licensure examinations and through regulatory measures, programs and activities that foster their professional growth and development." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 2)

q: Besides planning, designing, structural conceptualization, and specifying, Sec. 3(3) says 'General Practice of Architecture' also covers what?
o: Only preparing real estate appraisals
Exclusively teaching architecture at universities
Supervising and giving general administration and responsible direction to the erection, enlargement, or alteration of buildings and building environments
Solely selling construction materials
n: Section 3(3) defines General Practice of Architecture to include "supervising and giving general administration and responsible direction to the erection, enlargement or alterations of buildings and building environments and architectural design in engineering structures or any part thereof." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(3))

q: Sec. 13(d) requires an examination applicant to establish what?
o: Having taught architecture for at least two years
Having published at least one design in a journal
Having passed a foreign licensure exam
Never having been convicted of a criminal offense involving moral turpitude
n: Section 13(d) requires the applicant to establish "that he/she has not been convicted of any criminal offensive involving moral turpitude." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 13(d))

q: How is the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture composed, per Sec. 4?
o: Five members with no designated chairman
A chairman and two (2) members
A chairman and four (4) members
A chairman and six (6) regional members
n: Section 4 creates the Board "to be composed of a chairman and two (2) members appointed by the President of the Philippines." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 4)

q: Does RA 9266 affect or prevent the practice of other legally recognized professions, per Sec. 43?
o: Yes, it absorbs allied professions into architecture
Yes, but only regarding civil engineering
The Act is silent on the matter
No — Sec. 43 expressly says the Act shall not be construed to affect or prevent the practice of any other legally recognized profession
n: Section 43 states "this Act shall not be construed to affect or prevent the practice of any other legally recognized profession." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 43)

q: How does Sec. 3(10) describe a 'Service Agreement'?
o: A government permit required before construction starts
A certificate the Board issues upon passing the licensure exam
An informal verbal understanding between architect and client
A duly notarized written contract or equivalent public instrument stipulating the scope of services and guaranteeing compensation for a registered/licensed architect's services
n: Section 3(10) defines a "Service Agreement" as "a duly notarized written contract or equivalent public instrument stipulating the scope of services and guaranteeing compensation of such services to be rendered by an architect registered and licensed under this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(10))

q: Before entering practice, Sec. 17 requires all successful examination candidates to do what?
o: Pay an additional examination fee
Take an oath of profession before a Board member, an authorized government official, or anyone else legally authorized to administer oaths
Complete a one-year unpaid apprenticeship
Secure a DTI clearance
n: Section 17 requires successful candidates "to take an oath of profession before any member of the Board, any government official authorized by the Commission or any person authorized by law to administer oaths, prior to entering upon the practice of the profession." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 17)

q: One condition, per Sec. 38(a), for a foreign national to be granted a temporary/special permit is what?
o: Having already practiced in the Philippines ten years without a permit
Having passed the Philippine licensure exam in a prior year
Being a citizen/subject of a country that specifically permits Filipino professionals to practice there on the same basis as its own citizens
Being personally sponsored by a Board member
n: Section 38(a) requires that the foreign national "is a citizen or subject of a country which specifically permits Filipino professionals to practice his/her profession within their territorial limits, on the same basis as the subjects or citizens of such foreign state or country." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38(a))

q: Under Sec. 38(d), which two government offices must agencies/organizations/individuals engaging a foreign professional secure a special permit from?
o: DTI and SEC
PRC and DOLE
DFA and CHED
Bureau of Immigration and Bureau of Internal Revenue
n: Section 38(d) provides that such agencies, organizations or individuals "shall be responsible for securing a special permit from the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) and the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) pursuant to PRC and DOLE rules." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38(d))

q: Sec. 14 says the licensure examination covers, but is not limited to, how many subject groups?
o: Six (6)
Three (3)
Two (2)
Four (4)
n: Section 14 lists four subject groups: (1) History and Theory of Architecture/Principles of Planning and Architectural Practice; (2) Structural Design, Building Materials, Architectural Specifications, Methods of Construction and Utilities; (3) Urban Design and Architectural Interiors; and (4) Architectural Design and Site Planning. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 14)

q: A Board decision suspending or revoking a Certificate of Registration is subject to what recourse, with whose decision being final, per Sec. 23?
o: Appeal to the DTI
No recourse at all
Direct appeal to the Supreme Court
Appeal to the Commission
n: Section 23 provides "that such action of the Board shall be subject to appeal to the Commission whose decision shall be final." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23)

q: Per Sec. 3(2), what two documents, issued by the Board and Commission, does an 'Architect' hold?
o: A diploma and transcript of records
A tax identification number and barangay clearance
A business permit and mayor's clearance
A Certificate of Registration and a Professional Identification Card
n: Section 3(2) defines an Architect as a person "registered and licensed under this Act with a Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card issued by the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture and the Professional Regulation Commission." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(2))

q: Sec. 3(4)(e) says the scope of architecture practice expressly includes preparing which documents?
o: Building insurance actuarial tables
Environmental compliance certificates and land titles
Corporate income tax returns for construction firms
Architectural plans, specifications, bill of materials, cost estimates, general conditions, and bidding documents
n: Section 3(4)(e) includes within the scope of architecture practice "preparation of architectural plans, specifications, bill of materials, cost estimates, general conditions and bidding documents." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(e))

q: How does Sec. 3(12) define 'Continuing Professional Development' (CPD)?
o: A grading system used only for Board members
A mandatory annual re-examination identical to the licensure exam
A one-time refresher seminar taken only before retirement
A sustaining, progressive learning process that maintains, enhances, or increases architects' knowledge and continuing ability
n: Section 3(12) defines CPD as "a sustaining and progressive learning process that maintains, enhances, or increases the knowledge and continuing ability of architects." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(12))

q: What must the Board's annual report to the Commission cover, per Sec. 11?
o: Only the list of failing examinees
A five-year strategic plan for architecture education
Only the Board's annual budget request
A detailed account of its yearly proceedings, plus any recommendations it deems proper
n: Section 11 requires the Board to submit an annual report "giving a detailed account of its proceedings during the year and making such recommendations as it may deem proper." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 11)

q: Given the ratings above, has the examinee passed under Sec. 15?
o: No, because her Structural Design grade of 68% falls below the 70% general-average threshold
Yes, but only if she retakes Structural Design
No, because a general average alone is never enough regardless of subject grades
Yes — her weighted general average of 73% meets the required 70%, and no individual subject grade fell below 50%
n: Section 15 requires "a weighted general average of seventy percent (70%), with no grade lower than fifty percent (50%) in any given subject." Her 73% average meets the 70% threshold, and no subject grade is below 50%, so she passes. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 15)
scenario: A licensure examinee earns these subject ratings: History and Theory of Architecture, 78%; Structural Design, Building Materials, Specifications, Construction and Utilities, 68%; Urban Design and Architectural Interiors, 74%; Architectural Design and Site Planning, 72%. Her resulting weighted general average is 73%.

q: An architect signs plans actually prepared under another architect's supervision, without noting which parts he/she performed. Is this lawful under Sec. 20(3)?
o: Yes, signing a colleague's work is always allowed between architects
No, but only for government projects
Yes, if the supervising architect verbally consents

No — Sec. 20(3) bars signing/sealing such plans unless the signature clearly shows the part(s) the signer actually performed, and bars anyone but the architect-of-record from signing for work not actually done by them
n: Section 20(3) provides it is unlawful for an architect to sign or affix a seal on plans made under another architect's supervision "unless the same is made in such manner as to clearly indicate the part or parts of such work actually performed by the former," and unlawful for any person except the architect-of-record to sign for work not actually performed. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20(3))

q: Sec. 7(f) empowers the Board to monitor conditions affecting architecture practice and to do what else?
o: Certify structural safety in place of licensed engineers
Set nationwide construction-material prices
Prosecute criminal cases directly in court without the Commission
Adopt measures deemed proper for enhancing and maintaining high professional, ethical, and technical standards
n: Section 7(f) empowers the Board to "monitor the conditions affecting the practice of architecture and adopt such measures as may be deemed proper for the enhancement and maintenance of high professional, ethical and technical standards of the profession." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(f))

q: One of the Board's specific powers under Sec. 7(b) is to do what?
o: Elect the president of the integrated organization
Approve local-government building permits
Set the national infrastructure budget
Supervise the registration, licensure, and practice of architects
n: Section 7(b) empowers the Board to "supervise the registration, licensure and practice of architects." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(b))

q: Sec. 3(7) defines 'Authorship' as referring to those in charge of preparing plans/specifications, made how?
o: Exclusively via a computer-aided design program
By any unlicensed drafter, supervised or not
By the client's in-house engineering staff only
By them personally, or under their immediate supervision
n: Section 3(7) defines "Authorship" as referring to those in charge of preparing the plans or specifications, "whether made by them personally or under their immediate supervision." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(7))

q: Per Sec. 7(h), an unappealed Board administrative decision becomes final and executory after how many days from receipt of the notice?
o: Ten (10) days
Thirty (30) days
Fifteen (15) days
Sixty (60) days
n: Section 7(h) provides "the decision of the Board shall, unless appealed to the Commission, become final and executory after fifteen (15) days from receipt of notice of judgment or decision." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(h))

q: What short title does RA 9266 carry?
o: The Architects' Code of the Philippines
The Professional Architects Act
The Architecture Act of 2004
The Philippine Architecture Regulation Act
n: Section 1 of RA 9266 states: "This Act shall be known as 'The Architecture Act of 2004.'" (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 1)

q: An architect signs and seals plans he/she neither prepared nor supervised directly. Per Sec. 23(a), what results?
o: Only a civil matter between architect and client
A ground for the Board to suspend/revoke the certificate/PIC, subject to appeal to the Commission
Automatic permanent disbarment with no appeal
No consequence, as long as the plans are structurally sound
n: Section 23(a) makes it a ground for suspension or revocation where the architect "has signed and affixed or permitted to be signed or affixed his name or seal on architectural plans and designs, specification, drawings, technical reports, valuation, estimates, or other similar documents or work not prepared by him/her or not executed under his/her immediate supervision," subject to appeal to the Commission. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23(a))

q: What specific power does Sec. 7(e) grant the Board?
o: Printing its own currency for exam fees
Adopting an official seal of the Board
Granting honorary architecture degrees
Appointing judges to the Court of Appeals
n: Section 7(e) empowers the Board to "adopt an official seal of the Board." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(e))

q: Besides the integrated professional organization developing a CPD program, who else, per Sec. 28, may become CPD providers?
o: Only foreign universities
No other entity may ever provide CPD
Only the Commission itself
Other entities or organizations, once accredited by the Board
n: Section 28 provides "other entities or organizations may become CPD providers upon accreditation by the Board." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 28)

q: Upon conviction for practicing architecture without registration/license, Sec. 29 (Prohibition and Penal Clause) sets what fine range?
o: Not less than P10,000.00 but not more than P100,000.00
A flat fine of exactly P50,000.00, no range
Not less than P500,000.00 but not more than P10,000,000.00
Not less than P100,000.00 but not more than P5,000,000.00
n: Section 29 imposes "a fine of not less than One hundred thousand pesos (P100,000.00) but not more than Five Million pesos (P5,000,000.00) or...imprisonment for a period not less than six (6) months or not exceeding six (6) years, or both, at the discretion of the Court." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29)

q: A Board member is shown to have tolerated another registrant's violation of the Code of Ethical Conduct/Standards of Professional Practice. Is this valid grounds for suspension or removal under Sec. 9(b)?
o: No, tolerance of another's violation cannot be attributed to a Board member
No, only the registrant who violated it can be penalized
Yes, but only if repeated at least three times
Yes — Sec. 9(b) expressly names violating or tolerating a violation of the Act, its IRR, or the Code/Standards as a ground
n: Section 9(b) lists as a ground for suspension or removal "violation of tolerance of the violation of this Act, or its implementing rules and regulations or the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 9(b))

q: Under Sec. 47 (Effectivity), the Act takes effect how many days after publication in the Official Gazette or two newspapers of general circulation?
o: Thirty (30) days
Sixty (60) days
Ten (10) days
Fifteen (15) days
n: Section 47 states "this Act shall take effect after fifteen 15 (5) days following its publication in the Official Gazette or in two (2) newspapers of general circulation" — the operative period is fifteen (15) days. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 47)

q: Sec. 3(4)(j) covers 'all other works... which require the professional competence of an architect,' naming which two examples?
o: Managing hospital operations and running clinical trials
Practicing law and accounting
Conducting geological surveys and mineral exploration
Teaching architectural subjects and architectural computer-aided design
n: Section 3(4)(j) covers "all other works, projects and activities which require the professional competence of an architect, including teaching of architectural subjects and architectural computer-aided design." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(j))

q: Which power, listed under Sec. 7(c), belongs to the Board?
o: Deputizing the Philippine National Police for enforcement
Administering oaths in connection with the Act's administration
Imposing real property taxes on architectural firms
Appointing the DTI Secretary
n: Section 7(c) grants the Board power to "administer oaths in connection with the administration of this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(c))

q: An architect openly solicits and performs architectural work for a client without first signing a valid service agreement guaranteeing compensation. What may the Board do, per Sec. 23(e)?
o: Refer the matter exclusively to the DTI
Suspend or revoke the architect's Certificate of Registration/PIC, since this is a listed ground for suspension or revocation
Only give a verbal warning, no further action
Nothing, since a service agreement is merely optional
n: Section 23(e) lists as a ground for suspension or revocation having "openly solicited projects by actually undertaking architectural services without a valid service agreement guaranteeing compensation of services to be rendered." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23(e))

q: Which broad catch-all ground for suspension/revocation appears under Sec. 23(f)?
o: Having practiced architecture for more than 25 years
Having declined a project over a conflict of interest
Having violated any provision of the Act, its IRR, or the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice
Having designed a building that later needed renovation
n: Section 23(f) lists as a ground for suspension or revocation that the registrant "has violated any provision of this Act, its implementing rules and regulations, the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23(f))

q: Beyond citizenship, what personal qualification must an examination applicant establish, per Sec. 13(b)?
o: Good moral character
Having passed a separate government aptitude test
Being at least 30 years old
Having no outstanding student loans
n: Section 13(b) requires the applicant to establish "that he/she is of good moral character." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 13(b))

q: Even without using the title 'Architect,' Sec. 34 bars a non-registered person from doing what?
o: Selling construction materials to licensed architects
Claiming or representing their services/work as equivalent to a duly qualified registered architect's, or being qualified for any branch/function of architectural practice
Working at a construction site in any capacity
Attending architecture-related seminars
n: Section 34 provides that non-registered persons "shall not claim nor represent either services or work as equivalent to those of a duly qualified registered architect, or that they are qualified for any branch or functions of function of architectural practice, even though no form of the title 'Architect' is used." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 34)

q: Which of these is included in Sec. 3(4)(g)'s scope of architecture practice?
o: Structural conceptualization of engineering works only
Issuing business permits for architectural firms
Conducting the architecture licensure exam

Planning, architectural lay-outing and space utilization within/around buildings, including housing design, community architecture, interiors, space planning, detailing, lighting, acoustics, and lay-outing of mechanical/electrical/electronic/sanitary/plumbing/communications and other utility systems
n: Section 3(4)(g) covers "the planning, architectural lay-outing and utilization of spaces within and surrounding such buildings or structures, housing design and community architecture, architectural interiors and space planning, architectural detailing, architectural lighting, acoustics, architectural lay-outing of mechanical, electrical, electronic, sanitary, plumbing, communications and other utility systems, equipment and fixtures." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(g))

q: What full descriptive title does RA 9266's enacting clause give the law?
o: An Act establishing minimum wage standards for licensed architects
An Act creating the Department of Architecture of the Philippines
An Act abolishing the licensure exam for architects
An Act providing for a more responsive and comprehensive regulation for the registration, licensing, and practice of architecture, repealing Republic Act No. 545 as amended, and for other purposes
n: RA 9266's full title describes it as "AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MORE RESPONSIVE AND COMPREHENSIVE REGULATION FOR THE REGISTRATION, LICENSING AND PRACTICE OF ARCHITECTURE, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 545, AS AMENDED...AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES." (Source: RA 9266, Title/Enacting Clause)

q: Suppose instead her Structural Design grade were 48% while her weighted general average still worked out to 71%. Would she pass under Sec. 15?
o: No, since the general average must reach at least 75% regardless of subject grades
Yes, since her 71% weighted general average exceeds the 70% minimum
Yes, because under the Act only the general average matters, not individual subject grades
No — even though her 71% average exceeds 70%, a 48% subject grade falls below the 50% minimum required per subject, so she fails
n: Section 15 requires both a 70% weighted general average AND no grade lower than 50% in any given subject; a 48% subject grade fails that second condition regardless of the overall average. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 15)
scenario: Consider an examination candidate whose subject scores are: History and Theory of Architecture — 78%; Structural Design, Building Materials, Specifications, Construction and Utilities — 68%; Urban Design and Architectural Interiors — 74%; Architectural Design and Site Planning — 72%, yielding a weighted general average of 73%.

q: Per Sec. 14, is 'Urban Design and Architectural Interiors' grouped with any other topic under the same numbered subject item?
o: It's grouped with History and Theory of Architecture
It's combined with Architectural Design and Site Planning as one subject
It's grouped with Structural Design and Building Materials
It stands alone as its own subject group, item (3)
n: Section 14(3) lists "Urban Design and Architectural Interiors" as its own subject grouping, distinct from item (4) "Architectural Design and Site Planning." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 14(3))

q: Sec. 3(5) defines 'Structural Conceptualization' as conceiving and developing a structure's elements with due regard to what?
o: Only the facade's aesthetic appeal
Only compliance with foreign building codes
Only the lowest possible material cost, safety aside
Safety, cost-effectiveness, functionality, and aesthetics
n: Section 3(5) defines Structural Conceptualization as giving due consideration to "safety, cost-effectiveness, functionality and aesthetics." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(5))

q: Which power is named among the Board's functions under Sec. 7(m)?
o: Fixing retail prices of construction materials
Adopting a program for full computerization of the licensure exam
Setting the national minimum wage for architects
Issuing business permits for architectural firms
n: Section 7(m) empowers the Board "to adopt a program for the full computerization of the licensure examination." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(m))

q: An unlicensed contractor knowingly allows the use of plans prepared by a firm not duly licensed to practice architecture. Does Sec. 29's penal clause reach this?
o: No, only the unlicensed drafter, not those who merely use the plans, is covered
No, this falls only under the National Building Code, not RA 9266
Yes, but only if the contractor is a foreigner
Yes — Sec. 29 also penalizes anyone who knowingly allows the use, adoption, or implementation of plans made by an unlicensed person, firm, partnership, or company
n: Section 29 penalizes "any person whether Filipino or foreigner, who knowingly allows the use, adoption, implementation of plans, designs or specification made by any person, firm, partnership or company not duly licensed to engage in the practice of architecture." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29)

q: Under Sec. 44, whose primary duty is it to enforce the Act effectively, with law-enforcement assistance available on request?
o: The local barangay captains alone
The SEC alone
The DTI alone
The Commission and the Board
n: Section 44 states "it shall be the primary duty of the Commission and the Board to effectively enforce the provision of this Act," with law enforcement agencies rendering assistance upon call or request. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 44)

q: What do the abbreviations 'DTI' and 'SEC' stand for under Sec. 3(13)-(14)?
o: Department of Trade and Industry; Securities and Exchange Commission
Department of Tourism and Investment; Society of Engineers and Contractors
Department of Technical Instruction; Standards Enforcement Commission
Design and Technology Institute; Secretariat of Education and Commerce
n: Section 3(13) provides "DTI" shall mean the Department of Trade and Industry, and Section 3(14) provides "SEC" shall mean the Securities and Exchange Commission. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(13)-(14))

q: Per Sec. 20(2), a city/municipal officer enforcing building-construction laws must refuse to accept, approve, or pay for architectural plans not what?
o: Notarized by a lawyer
Translated into English
Printed on government-issued paper
Prepared and submitted fully in accord with the Act's provisions, signed and sealed by the author
n: Section 20(2) prohibits government officers from accepting or approving plans "which have not been prepared and submitted in full accord with all the provisions of this Act," or approving payment for work not "signed and sealed by the author." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20(2))

q: Beyond the Certificate of Registration/PIC and their dates, what other number must an architect show on professional documents, per Sec. 21?
o: The architect's voter's ID number
The professional tax receipt (PTR) number
The architect's SSS number
The architect's home telephone number
n: Section 21 requires an architect to indicate the Certificate of Registration and PIC details "including the professional tax receipt number, on the documents he/she signs, uses or issues." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 21)

q: How does Sec. 10 set the compensation and allowances of the Board's chairman and members?
o: Limited only to per diem, no salary
Paid directly by the integrated professional organization
Fixed permanently at the 2004 rate with no future adjustment
Comparable to other regulatory boards under the Commission, per the General Appropriations Act
n: Section 10 provides Board compensation "comparable to that being received by the chairman and members of existing regulatory Boards under the Commission as provided for in the General Appropriations Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 10)

q: What do 'Board' and 'Commission' respectively mean under Sec. 3(8) and (9)?
o: 'Board' means the Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization
'Board' means the PRC; 'Commission' means the Board of Architecture
'Board' means the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture; 'Commission' means the Professional Regulation Commission
Both terms refer interchangeably to the DTI
n: Section 3(8) provides that "Board" refers to the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture, while Section 3(9) provides that "Commission" means the Professional Regulation Commission. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(8)-(9))

q: Per Sec. 42, into what document must the Commission's Chairperson fold the funding for implementing the Act?
o: The Board's private trust fund
The integrated organization's membership-dues schedule
The annual General Appropriations Act
A special foreign grant application
n: Section 42 provides that the Chairperson of the Commission shall include implementation of the Act in Commission programs, "the funding of which shall be included in the annual General Appropriations Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 42)

q: What must the roster the Board prepares and updates under Sec. 19 show?
o: Only architects who failed the licensure exam
Only the names of foreign architects with temporary permits
Only the names of past Board members
The names and place of business of all registered professional architects, made available to any party as needed
n: Section 19 requires "a roster showing the names and place of business of all registered professional architects...prepared and updated by the Board and copies thereof shall be made available to any party as may be deemed necessary." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 19)

q: A Board member discloses secret and confidential exam questions before the exam takes place. Is this valid grounds for suspension or removal under Sec. 9?
o: No, disclosure of exam questions is purely an internal disciplinary matter
No, only a criminal conviction is a valid ground for removal
Yes, but only if proven in criminal court first
Yes — Sec. 9(d) names manipulating/rigging exam results and disclosing secret/confidential exam information as a ground
n: Section 9(d) lists as a ground for suspension or removal "manipulation or rigging of the architecture licensure examination results, disclosure of secret and confidential information in the examination questions prior to the conduct of the said examination or tampering of grades." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 9(d))

q: No one may practice architecture, prepare building plans, or use the title 'Architect' in the country unless, per Sec. 25, they have received what from the Board?
o: A diploma in architecture from any recognized school
A local-government business permit only
Membership in a private professional club
A Certificate of Registration and a Professional Identification Card, issued as the Act provides
n: Section 25 requires that a person "shall have received from the Board a Certificate of Registration and be issued a Professional Identification Card in the manner hereinafter provided" before practicing architecture or using the title "Architect." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 25)

q: Under Sec. 37(a), who may form and register a firm to practice architecture, alone or with allied technical professionals?
o: Any foreign national residing in the Philippines
Only Filipino citizens properly registered and licensed as architects under the Act
Only civil engineers, without any architect involved
Any corporation, regardless of its incorporators' profession
n: Section 37(a) provides "only Filipino citizens properly registered and licensed as architects under this Act may, among themselves, or together with allied technical professionals, form and obtain registration as a firm, company, partnership, association or corporation for the practice of architecture." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 37(a))

q: Sec. 20(4) treats duly signed, stamped, or sealed drawings and specifications, as instruments of service, as what?
o: The contractor's exclusive property
Public-domain material free for anyone to copy
Government property once a building permit issues
The architect's intellectual property and documents, whether or not the depicted object is ever built
n: Section 20(4) states such drawings "are the intellectual properties and documents of the architect, whether the object for which they are made is executed or not," and prohibits unauthorized duplication or copying. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20(4))

q: A newly organized Board wants to make CPD attendance mandatory before renewing licenses. Does Sec. 7(i) allow this?
o: Yes, but only for architects under 40
Yes, CPD attendance is an absolute renewal prerequisite
No, the Board has no authority over CPD whatsoever
No — Sec. 7(i) expressly says CPD attendance shall not be a mandatory requirement for license renewal
n: Section 7(i) authorizes the Board to prescribe CPD guidelines but expressly provides "that the attendance to said CPD shall not be a mandatory requirement for the renewal of a professional license." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(i))

q: An architect's Certificate of Registration expired six months ago and was never renewed. Under Sec. 20(1), may he lawfully keep stamping documents with his seal?
o: Yes, the seal stays valid indefinitely once issued
No, but only if a client formally complains
Yes, so long as he pays a late-renewal penalty afterward
No — it is unlawful to stamp/seal documents with the seal once the certificate has expired or been revoked, unless renewed or re-issued
n: Section 20(1) makes it "unlawful for any one to stamp or seal any documents with said seal after the certificate of the registrant named thereon has expired or has been revoked, unless said certificate shall have been renewed or re-issued." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20(1))

q: Sec. 5(c) requires a Board nominee to have held a valid Certificate of Registration/PIC and actively practiced for at least how many years by the appointment date?
o: Five (5) years
Ten (10) years
Fifteen (15) years
Seven (7) years
n: Section 5(c) requires a Board member to "be an architect with a valid Certificate of Registration and Professional Identification Card and active practitioner of architecture for at least ten (10) years on the date of his/her appointment." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 5(c))

q: Within how many months of the Act's effectivity must the Board be organized, per Sec. 4?
o: Six (6) months
One (1) year
Two (2) years
Three (3) months
n: Section 4 states: "The Board shall be organized not later than six (6) months from the effectivity of this Act." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 4)

q: A non-Filipino applying for the licensure exam must prove his/her country does what for Filipino architects, per Sec. 27?
o: Requires Filipino architects to pay a special foreign tax first
Bars Filipino architects from ever practicing there

Admits Filipino citizens to the profession without restriction, or lets them practice after examination on terms of strict and absolute equality, including unconditional recognition of Philippine degrees
Grants a Philippine license automatically, without examination
n: Section 27's reciprocity requirement obliges the foreign applicant to prove his country "admits citizens of the Philippines to the practice of the same profession without restriction or allows them to practice it after passing an examination on terms of strict and absolute equality...including the unconditional recognition of prerequisite degrees/diplomas." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 27)

q: Which subject rounds out the four examination subjects listed under Sec. 14(4)?
o: Building Code Enforcement and Zoning Law
Interior Design and Furniture Fabrication
Architectural Design and Site Planning
Quantity Surveying and Cost Estimation
n: Section 14(4) lists "Architectural Design and Site Planning" as one of the subjects for the licensure examination. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 14(4))

q: In reinstating a revoked Certificate of Registration, may the Board, per Sec. 24, exempt the applicant from a new licensure exam?
o: Yes — the Board may, at its discretion, grant this exemption
Only foreign architects may receive such an exemption
No, a new exam is always mandatory for reinstatement
Only the Commission, never the Board, may grant this exemption
n: Section 24 states the Board "may, in its discretion, exempt the applicant from taking another examination" when reinstating a revoked Certificate of Registration. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 24)

q: Given the 100-person ownership scenario above, what is the minimum number who must be registered and licensed architects for the firm to lawfully register, per Sec. 37(b)?
o: At least 25 (25%)
At least 75 (75%)
At least 50 (50%)
n: Section 37(b) requires that "registered and licensed architects shall compose at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the owners, shareholders, members, incorporators, directors, executive officers, as the case may be." Seventy-five percent of 100 is 75. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 37(b))
scenario: Scenario: An architectural firm organizing as a corporation counts a combined total of 100 people among its owners, shareholders, incorporators, directors, and executive officers.

q: What do the Board's powers under Sec. 7(a) and (g) include?
o: Only hearing criminal cases filed in regular courts
Setting foreign-exchange rates for imported architectural materials
Only administering the licensure exam, without rule-making authority
Prescribing/adopting rules and regulations to carry out the Act, and prescribing/adopting the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice
n: Section 7(a) empowers the Board to "prescribe and adopt the rules and regulations necessary for carrying out the provisions of this Act," and Section 7(g) to "prescribe and/or adopt the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(a), (g))

q: How does Sec. 3(1) define 'Architecture'?
o: The trade of assembling prefabricated building components
The exclusive act of preparing structural computations for buildings
The business of managing real estate development projects
The art, science, or profession of planning, designing, and constructing buildings in their totality, considering their environment, per the principles of utility, strength, and beauty
n: Section 3(1) defines Architecture as "the art, science or profession of planning, designing and constructing buildings in their totality taking into account their environment, in accordance with the principles of utility, strength and beauty." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(1))

q: Sec. 5(a) requires a Board-member appointee to be what, at the time of appointment?
o: A citizen and resident of the Philippines
A holder of a law degree in addition to architecture
A Metro Manila resident for at least 20 years
A member of the House of Representatives
n: Section 5(a) requires each Board member to "be a citizen and resident of the Philippines." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 5(a))

q: Beyond preparing/adopting/amending exam syllabi, what else does Sec. 7(j) empower the Board to do?
o: Set exam fees without limit or approval
Waive the exam automatically for foreign-trained applicants
Delegate the entire exam process to private review centers
Determine and prepare questions within the syllabi's scope, and administer, correct, and release licensure exam results
n: Section 7(j) empowers the Board to "prepare, adopt, issue or amend the syllabi of the subjects for examinations by determining and preparing questions...as well as administer, correct and release the results of the licensure examinations." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(j))

q: An architect with exceptional or recognized expertise in a specific branch of architecture, engaged for that specialization, is called what under RA 9266?
o: Integrated architect
Architecture-in-charge of construction
Architect-of-record
Consulting Architect
n: Section 3(2)(c) defines "Consulting Architect" as an architect "with exceptional or recognized expertise or specialization in any branch of architecture." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(2)(c))

q: Sec. 7(n)'s catch-all power lets the Board discharge other duties deemed necessary for what purpose?
o: Transferring Board functions to local government units
Abolishing the integrated professional organization
Enhancing the architecture profession and upgrading/developing/growing architecture education
Privatizing the licensure exam process
n: Section 7(n) empowers the Board to "discharge such other duties and functions as may be deemed necessary for the enhancement of the architecture profession and the upgrading, development and growth of the architecture education." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7(n))

q: Sec. 3(4)(f)'s 'construction and project management' scope covers general management, administration, supervision, coordination, and responsible direction over what activities?
o: Only hiring and payroll of construction laborers
Only project financing and loan processing
Only marketing and advertising the finished building
Planning, architectural designing, construction, reconstruction, erection, enlargement/demolition, renovation, repair, remodeling, alteration, preservation, or restoration of buildings/structures
n: Section 3(4)(f) lists "construction and project management, giving general management, administration, supervision, coordination and responsible direction or the planning, architectural designing, construction, reconstruction, erection, enlargement or demolition, renovation, repair, orderly removal, remodeling, alteration, preservation or restoration of buildings or structures" as part of the scope of practice. (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(f))

q: Under Sec. 37(d), a firm, partnership, association, or corporation practicing architecture must register with which two entities?
o: The integrated professional organization only
The Bureau of Internal Revenue and CHED
The DTI and the local government unit
The Securities and Exchange Commission and the Board
n: Section 37(d) requires "such firm, partnership, association or corporation shall be registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission and Board." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 37(d))

q: After how many years from revocation may the Board, on application and for reasons it deems proper and sufficient, reinstate a revoked Certificate of Registration, per Sec. 24?
o: Two (2) years
Three (3) years
Five (5) years
One (1) year
n: Section 24 provides the Board may act "after the expiration of two (2) years from the date of revocation of a Certificate of Registration, Professional Identification Card or special/temporary permit." (Source: RA 9266, Sec. 24)
